atomic_comments.content: The paper lacks sufficient experimental evidence to support the claim that UniSim can simulate low-level actions well.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: I believe it might need more experimental evidence to support the claim that it can simulate low-level actions well.

atomic_comments.content: The experiments in section 4.2 are limited to simple object rearrangement on a table, without testing more complex low-level actions like grasping or pulling.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: section 4.2 only shows results for a relatively simple object (mostly blocks) re-arrangement (without grasping, e.g.) on a table.

atomic_comments.content: The work should include experiments on more complex low-level actions, such as grasping objects and pulling objects (e.g., opening a drawer).
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: What about grasping objects, pulling objects (e.g., opening a drawer), etc?

atomic_comments.content: Testing more complex low-level actions would provide insights into the fine-grained control capabilities of the simulator.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: It will give us insights as to how fine-grained the controls are supported by the proposed simulator

atomic_comments.content: The reviewer questions whether the simulator can handle more complex low-level actions beyond simple rearrangement, referencing the weakness section.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: See “weaknesses”

atomic_comments.content: The title and framing are too general and risk feeling showy, not specific to this paper.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The title is very general, and applies to any paper on model-based RL for the real-world rather than something specific to this paper, and naming the method a "universal simulator" feels grandiose.

atomic_comments.content: Highlighting POMDP connection as a main contribution is not appropriate as it is assumed by any world model paper.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The connection between POMDP's and action-conditioned video generation is more-or-less assumed by any world model paper (e.g. [1]), and shouldn't be highlighted as a main contribution of the paper.

atomic_comments.content: The claim about novelty from dataset mixture lacks hard evidence.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Yet no hard evidence is given for this combination being important -- aside from two vague figures in Appendix E.

atomic_comments.content: Train and evaluate a version of UniSim on single-environment data to show the value of dataset diversity.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: At a minimum, it would be important to train a version of UniSim on say, datasets from the Language Table environment _only_ , and report numbers for when synthetic data was generated from this, in Table 2 and 3.

atomic_comments.content: It is unclear if actions (e.g., camera commands) can generalize to new video domains.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: For example, could camera commands (zoom in etc) successfully be applied to kitchen scenes as in Figure 3? The fact that the name of the dataset had to be included as part of the action during training, makes me suspect actions may not be able to generalise well to new kinds of video.

atomic_comments.content: The paper lacks strong baselines and sufficient ablation studies.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: A lack of strong baselines might be expected for this kind of scale-up work. But in their absence, ablations become more important, to verify that the various components of the model were all necessary. The paper only presents a brief study of which frames to condition on.

atomic_comments.content: The model section is poorly written, with misleading notation and unclear explanations.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The model section is poorly written. The use of $\mathcal{T}$ is (I think) slightly misleading ... I also didn't understand why the model conditions on the noised, rather than clean, previous observations.

atomic_comments.content: Shift key model details from the appendix to the main body for better readability.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: It's a shame to give the model details only in the Appendix C, as I believe many readers would be interested in them. I hope some of these can be shifted to the main body, particularly key details around the diffusion architecture.

atomic_comments.content: The algorithmic or model novelty is minimal, relying on straightforward video diffusion.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Any algorithmic or model novelty is light (more or less straightforward video diffusion).

atomic_comments.content: The main experiments are only on environments within the training distribution, lacking out-of-distribution evaluation.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The two main experiments were conducted on environments that were within the training distribution of UniSim. It would have been more impressive to investigate the performance on new environments.

atomic_comments.content: Replace the verbose dataset description in Section 2.1 with a reference to the concise table in the appendix.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: The wordy description of all datasets in 2.1, I felt was much better summarized by Table 5 in the Appendix ... and might be swapped.

atomic_comments.content: The ratio of training updates to compute seems low; did performance saturate?
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Appendix says 1M steps on 512 TPUs with batchsize 256 -- this seemed a low ratio of training updates to available compute. Did performance saturate beyond this?

atomic_comments.content: Asks for the wall clock time of the model training.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: What was the wall clock time of the model training?

atomic_comments.content: Asks for the number of parameters in the model.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: How many parameters were in the model?

atomic_comments.content: Asks if the model weights will be open-sourced.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Will the model weights be open-sourced?

atomic_comments.content: The model's generalization across different embodiments is questioned, as generated videos appear to stay within the distribution of their training data (e.g., robotic scenes look like the robotic dataset, human scenes handle only human hands).
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: the shown demo looks like generally still in distribution, in terms of generalization across different embodiment

atomic_comments.content: The reviewer asks how the model would work in complex scenes when commanded to predict outcomes given a robot action input, given the observed limitations.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: How does it work in those complex scenes when the model is commanded to predict outcomes given a robot action input?

atomic_comments.content: The paper seems to only handle delta motion in Cartesian space for low-level control, lacking handling of more general end-effector actions in SE3 space.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: the paper seems only handling delta motion in the cartesion space. Does it handle more general end- effector action in SE3 space?

atomic_comments.content: The reviewer questions whether predicting outcomes conditioned on robot action requires the robot arm to be visible in the first frame.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Is it true that for predicting outcomes conditioned on robot action, the robot arm needs to be visible in the first place?

atomic_comments.content: The research direction and proposed method are considered very cool and impressive.
atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Very cool and impressive research direction and proposed method

atomic_comments.anchor_quote: Huge effort devoted in unifying multiple large scale datasets
